ideas.description: Reallocate time from full-res epochs to cheap low-res epochs. The Muon epoch slope at the knee is now steep (~1.14 pp/epoch, ~0.15 pp per 1% time). E013 priced 24 px epochs at only ~0.058 pp per 1% on SGD, so low-res epochs should now be cheaper than full-res ones. On the tip (E034 commit f74c715: Muon NS3 batched, lr 0.16, mom 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, LS 0.2, SiLU, whitening bias trained only in epoch 1, ~6.5 epochs), make one curriculum change. Train the first 1.5 epochs on whole images bilinearly downsampled to 24 px (F.interpolate, antialias=True, inside the compiled GPU augment, after flip/translate). Then train 5.25 epochs at 32 px, for 6.75 epochs total. Scale the lr, Muon and lookahead schedules to the new total step count; bs stays 1024. The frozen whitening conv is reused unchanged. In drafts/, first print the per-block spatial sizes at 24 px input. Set the final pool for each resolution graph to F.max_pool2d with a static kernel equal to that graph's final map size. Do NOT use amax or flatten().max (the E009 Inductor bug). Compile and warm up every variant in build() on synthetic data: 24 px with whitening-bias grad, 24 px without it, 32 px without it, plus each full and partial batch shape. Eval stays the 32 px graph. Run drafts/debug_nan.py on every graph under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs before launching.
ideas.expected: Time -3% to -7%, point -5% (~5.6 s vs 5.894 s): 1.5 epochs at ~0.53 s plus 5.25 at ~0.89 s, against 6.5 at ~0.89 s. Accuracy -0.7 to +0.3 pp, point -0.15 pp (~0.7535), if a low-res early epoch is worth ~75% of a full one. Feasible means a new best. If it is infeasible by <=0.2 pp, keep the code path and retry at 7.0 total epochs (first 1.75 at 24 px). A drop >=0.5 pp means early full-res steps matter under Muon; then refute H2.3.2 and close resolution work.

ideas.description: Batch-size ramp as a cheap form of lr decay (D008 C0091). Run this only after I042. Skip it if I042 (fixed bs 1536) holds accuracy within 0.15 pp, since fixed large batch then dominates. Run it if I042 drops more than 0.3 pp. On the tip, make one change: keep bs 1024 for the first 60% of training samples, then switch to bs 2048 for the last 40% (~127 tail steps become ~64). Total epochs are unchanged. All schedules (lr warmup and decay, Muon lr, lookahead decay ramp) become functions of the fraction of samples seen, not the step index, so per-step lr values at a given progress are unchanged. The Muon lr is unscaled, and the SGD group's per-step lr is unchanged; a larger batch at the same lr acts as a lower effective lr in the tail, where the lr is already decaying. Lookahead syncs every 5 steps as before. Compile and warm up the bs-2048 full and partial train-step shapes in build(). Run debug_nan.py on the new shape.
ideas.expected: Time -2% to -5%, point -3.5% (~5.69 s): ~63 fewer steps of Muon, SGD and lookahead overhead (~2 ms each) plus better GEMM efficiency at bs 2048 in the tail. Accuracy -0.5 to +0.15 pp, point -0.2 pp. The early, step-limited phase is untouched, so this should cost less than I042's fixed bs 1536. If the drop is <=0.15 pp, keep it (feasible at the 0.21 pp margin) and try switching at 50%. A drop >=0.35 pp means even the low-lr tail is step-limited here; then close the batch-size axis.

drop.reason: Its point estimate is -1.0%, below the ~1.5% single-run timing jitter (H4.1), so a win could not be distinguished from noise or kept. The batched, compiled Muon step (E023) already fuses the projection, so it is probably far below the 0.15 ms gate. It also changes the math, which adds re-draw risk at a 0.21 pp margin. H2.4.3 stays open, to be bundled later with another systems change.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is E034: 5.894 s at accuracy 0.7551, only ~0.21 pp above the gate. Epoch trimming without an accuracy gain is not viable: 0.25 epoch costs ~0.29 pp at the current slope.

I added two ideas:
- **Low-res curriculum (H2.3.2, priority 3).** Under Muon the full-res epoch slope (~0.15 pp per 1% time) is now roughly 2.5x E013's low-res price (~0.058 pp per 1%), so trading 1.25 full-res epochs for 1.5 cheap 24 px epochs could cut ~5% of time. The pool must use static per-resolution kernels to avoid the E009 amax bug.
- **Batch-size ramp (H1.2, priority 2).** bs 1024 for the first 60%, then bs 2048 in the tail. It only runs if I042's fixed bs 1536 loses accuracy. It keeps the step-limited early phase intact while cutting tail step overhead.

I dropped I045 (projection every k steps). Its expected -1% is inside timing jitter, and the projection is probably already fused into the compiled step.

The queue now holds 8 queued ideas: I039 (LS 0.1), I040 (block-1 depth traded for epochs), I041 (CUDA-graph Muon, gated), I042 (bs 1536), I043 (brightness/contrast jitter), I044 (head lr x0.5), plus the two new ones. That mix is mostly exploit (systems cuts and accuracy-margin tuning) with explore work on batch size, augmentation and resolution. Priority order: I040, I039, I044, I041, the low-res curriculum, then I042, I043 and the ramp.
